newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backeds firm ahead of retail sales, PPI.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backeds firm ahead of retail sales, PPI.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities were below session highs but up slightly in quiet afternoon dealings ahead of Wednesday's economic and inflation news.

There was some surprise among investors at the extent of the gains in the Treasury prices in the wake of the July Richmond Federal Reserve manufacturing shipments report, participants said. July manufacturing shipments fell to -10 from 15 in June.
"It has been fairly quiet, but some people may be surprised by the run-up" in Treasury prices, said a New York market observer.
Premium mortgage coupons were 1/32 to 3/32 firmer, while discount mortgage coupons were as much as 9/32 firmer.

Market players reported some buying of adjustable-rate mortgage product. Some participants said a list of COFI (Cost of Funds Indexed) adjustable-rate mortgage securities would be out for bid later in the day.
"If you are bearish (on Treasuries) then it's a more defensive instrument," a participant said. "It has a shorter duration, which means there is less downside if rates rise."
Meanwhile, participants were eagerly awaiting the July retail sales and Producer Price Index data due early Wednesday.

Current coupon bonds from Government National Mortgage Association were 3/32 firmer at 100 30/32 to yield 7.39 percent. Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp 7.5 percent coupons were up 6/32 at 101 8/32 to yield 7.32 percent. And, Fannie Mae 7.5 percent coupons were 4/32 firmer at 101 to yield 7.33 percent.
The 10-year Treasury note was 10/32 firmer at 98 17/32 to yield 6.33 percent.

Economists surveyed by Reuters expected data to show July retail sales rose 0.7 percent, or 0.5 percent excluding autos. They expected a July Producer Price Index increase of 0.1 percent, both for the headline number and the core which excludes food and energy.

"While we have inflation data this week, the retail sales report will set the tone for MBS this week," said a New York market player. People in the market, she said, were looking to assess consumer demand.

"If tomorrow's (retail sales ) number is as expected, we may fall into a trading range. If the number produces a rise in prices, it would cause the most difficulty for MBS investors," the New York market observer said.

Market players said the 10-year Treasury note rate would have to go to 6.20 percent to affect 8.0 percent and 8.5 percent coupons; the 10-year Treasury note would have to fall to 6.10 to affect 7.5 percent coupon prices.

Lower interest rates could erode cusp coupon and slightly higher coupon prices because they would resurrect fears of prepayments. In recent weeks, investors voiced concerns that lower interest rates could prompt homeowners to refinance their mortgage loans. Those prepayment fears induced some investors to move down in coupon or out of MBS into Treasuries.
